source_text: Tunc Agapius, qui iamdudum martyrio suo consummatae fidei sacramenta perfecerat, qui et ipse, cum pro puellis duabus, Tertulla et Antonia, quas sibi carissimas ad uicem pignerum diligebat, repetitis frequenter precibus oraret ut secum et illae dei dignatione martyres fierent, retulerat meritorum suorum tali reuelatione fiduciam. Cui dictum est: Quid assidue petis quod una oratione meruisti? Is ergo Agapius agenti Iacobo in carcere per tempus quietis apparuit. Nam sub ipso ictu passionis, dum expectatur carnifex, Et bene, inquit Iacobus, ad Agapii ceterorumque martyrum beatissimorum pergo conuiuium. Nam ista nocte, fratres, Agapium nostrum uidebam inter omnes alios laetiorem, quos una nobiscum Cirtensis carcer incluserat, sollemne quoddam et laetitiae plenum celebrare conuiuium. Quo cum ego et Marianus quasi ad agapem spiritu dilectionis et caritatis raperemur, adcucurrit nobis obuius puer, quem constabat esse alterum ex geminis ante triduum cum matre conpassis, corona rosea collo circumdatus et in manu dextera palmam uiridissimam praeferens, et Quid properatis? inquit, gaudete et exultate, cras enim nobiscum et ipsi caenabitis. O dei magna in suos et praeclara dignatio! O uera et paterna pietas in Iesu Christo domino nostro, qui dilectis suis et indulget tam larga beneficia et clementiae suae munera praestaturus ante declarat. Dies a uisione primus inluxerat, et iam promissis dei sententia praesidis seruiebat, quae Marianum et Iacobum et ceteros clericos tandem patriarchis cum gloria redditos, e pressuris saeculi sententia animaduersionis emisit. Nam perducti sunt ad coronae locum, qui riparum collibus hinc et inde sublimibus, media fluminis conualle subsederat; sed et spectaculo erat excelsa utrimque aggeris altitudo. Alueus ipse medio sinu cruorem beati sanguinis hauriebat. Nec deerat utriusque sacramenti genus, cum et baptizarentur suo sanguine et lauarentur in flumine.
pass_a_gloss: Then Agapius, who some time ago had fulfilled by his martyrdom the sacraments of completed faith, and who himself, when he was praying with often-repeated entreaties for the two girls Tertulla and Antonia, whom he loved as most dear in place of pledges, that they also with him might be made martyrs by God's condescension, had brought back confidence of his merits by such a revelation; to him it was said: Why do you continually seek what you have merited by one prayer? This Agapius therefore appeared to James acting in prison in the time of rest. For under the very stroke of suffering, while the executioner is awaited, James said: How well I go to the banquet of Agapius and the other most blessed martyrs. For this night, brothers, I was seeing our Agapius, more glad than all the others whom the Cirta prison had enclosed together with us, celebrating a certain solemn and joy-filled banquet; to which, when I and Marianus were being seized as to an agape by the spirit of love and charity, a boy ran up toward us, established to be one of the twins who had suffered three days earlier with their mother, bound round the neck with a rosy crown and presenting in his right hand a very green palm, and said: Why do you hasten? Rejoice and exult, for tomorrow you also will dine with us. O great and splendid condescension of God toward his own! O true and paternal mercy in Jesus Christ our Lord, who both grants to his beloved such generous benefits and declares in advance the gifts of his clemency that he is about to bestow. The first day from the vision had dawned, and already the sentence of the governor was serving the promises of God, which sent out Marian and James and the other clergy, at length restored with glory to the patriarchs, from the pressures of the world by a sentence of punishment. For they were led to the place of the crown, which had sunk down in the middle valley of a river with high hills of the banks on either side; but the lofty height of the slope on both sides served for viewing. The channel itself in its middle curve was drinking the stream of blessed blood. Nor was either kind of sacrament wanting, since they were both baptized in their own blood and washed in the river.
pass_b_english: Then Agapius, who had long since brought to its end, by his own martyrdom, the sacred mystery of a perfected faith, and who, while pleading with many repeated prayers for the two girls Tertulla and Antonia, whom he cherished as dearest in place of his own children, that they also might be made martyrs together with him by God's gracious favor, had received in such a revelation the assurance of his merits. To him it had been said: Why do you keep asking for what you have already obtained by a single prayer? This Agapius appeared to James while he took rest in prison. For beneath the very stroke of suffering, while the executioner was still awaited, James said: How fittingly I go to the feast of Agapius and the other most blessed martyrs. For this night, brothers, I was beholding our Agapius, more joyful than all the rest whom the prison at Cirta had shut in with us, keeping a solemn feast full of gladness, toward which I and Marianus were being drawn as to a love-feast by the spirit of affection and charity, when a boy hastened to meet us, known to be one of the twins who had suffered three days before with their mother, with a rose-red garland about his neck and bearing in his right hand a most verdant palm, and he said: Why do you hasten? Rejoice and exult (Matthew 5:12), for tomorrow you yourselves will feast with us. O how great and glorious is God's gracious favor toward his own! O how true and fatherly is the mercy in Jesus Christ our Lord, who both grants such lavish blessings to his beloved and makes known beforehand the gifts of his kindness which he is about to bestow.

The first day after the vision had dawned, and already the governor's sentence was serving the promises of God, which by its verdict of condemnation set Marianus and James and the other clergy free from the afflictions of the world, restored at last with glory to the patriarchs. For they were conducted to the place of the crown, which lay in the low valley of a stream between the lofty ridges of its banks on either side, and the towering height of the embankment on both sides furnished a natural amphitheatre. The channel itself in its middle hollow caught the flowing stream of their blessed blood. Nor was either kind of sacrament lacking, for they were both baptized in their own blood and washed clean in the river.
